title: Why You Should NEVER Hold in a Sneeze

scenes.name: The Violent Trap
scenes.narration: A sneeze expels air from your lungs at nearly one hundred miles per hour. But if you pinch your nose and mouth to stifle it...

scenes.name: The Rebounding Shockwave
scenes.narration: That violent blast has nowhere to go. It turns inward, skyrocketing the pressure inside your head by twenty-four times normal levels.

scenes.name: The Ruptured Eardrum
scenes.narration: The shockwave slams back into your Eustachian tubes, which can literally rupture your eardrums and cause permanent hearing loss.

scenes.name: Throat Muscle Tear
scenes.narration: Even worse, the extreme force can tear the delicate muscles in your throat, trapping dangerous air pockets inside your neck and chest.

scenes.name: Popped Blood Vessels
scenes.narration: The sudden pressure spike instantly surges into your eyes, popping microscopic blood vessels and leaving the whites bruised and bloody.

scenes.name: The Lethal Aneurysm Risk
scenes.narration: In severe cases, this intense pressure spike can even cause a weak brain artery to rupture, triggering a life-threatening aneurysm.

scenes.name: The Safe Resolution
scenes.narration: That's why doctors warn to never hold it in. Always sneeze freely into your elbow to let the pressure escape safely.
